source: scripts/dat-mock-bank.json (QR, five choices with a worked reason)

items.stem: A clinic sees 40 patients per day. The daily count rises 25 percent, and then the new count falls 20 percent. How many patients per day does the clinic see now?
items.why: Fastest: 1.25 x 0.8 = 1, so the count is back to 40. Full method: Step 1, up 25 percent: 40 x 1.25 = 50. Step 2, down 20 percent of 50, which is 10: 50 - 10 = 40. Takeaway: successive percents multiply; a 25 percent rise and a 20 percent fall exactly undo each other because 1.25 x 0.8 = 1.

items.stem: A recipe uses 2.5 cups of flour for 10 cookies. How many cups of flour are needed for 36 cookies?
items.why: Fastest: 36 cookies is 3.6 batches of 10, and 3.6 x 2.5 = 9 cups. Full method: flour per cookie = 2.5 / 10 = 0.25 cup; 36 cookies need 36 x 0.25 = 9 cups. (Proportion: 2.5/10 = x/36, so x = 9.) Takeaway: find the unit rate, then scale.

items.stem: A lab orders 19 boxes of gloves, and each box holds 98 gloves. About how many gloves is that?
items.why: Fastest: round the near-hundred: 98 is about 100, so 19 x 100 = 1,900. (Exactly 19 x 98 = 1,862.) Full method: 19 x 98 = 19 x (100 - 2) = 1,900 - 38 = 1,862, and the closest choice is 1,900. Takeaway: round to friendly numbers, and keep track of the zeros; choices on the DAT are often a factor of 10 apart.

items.stem: A pump moves 706 liters of water per hour. About how many liters does it move in 46 hours?
items.why: Fastest: 700 x 46 = 7 x 46 x 100 = 322 x 100 = 32,200, closest to 32,000. (Exactly 706 x 46 = 32,476.) Full method: round 706 to 700 and multiply: 32,200; the choice nearest the exact 32,476 is 32,000. Takeaway: round only the number that is close to a friendly value, and count zeros before you pick.

items.stem: A clinic network performs 2,192 cleanings per week. About how many cleanings does it perform in 69 weeks?
items.why: Fastest: 2,200 x 70 = 154,000, so about 150,000. (Exactly 2,192 x 69 = 151,248.) Full method: round both factors to friendly numbers near them, 2,200 and 70; their product, 154,000, sits closest to 150,000, and the exact product 151,248 confirms it. Takeaway: round each factor to its nearest friendly value, then check that no other choice is closer.

items.stem: Solve: 2x - 9 = -x + 10
items.why: Fastest: add x and add 9 in one move: 3x = 19, so x = 19/3 (about 6.33). Full method: Step 1, add x to both sides: 3x - 9 = 10. Step 2, add 9: 3x = 19. Step 3, divide by 3: x = 19/3. Check: 2(19/3) - 9 = 11/3 and -19/3 + 10 = 11/3. Takeaway: a term changes sign when it crosses the equals sign; keep the answer as a fraction until the end.

items.stem: Solve: 4x + 8 = x - 3
items.why: Fastest: subtract x and 8 in one move: 3x = -3 - 8 = -11, so x = -11/3 (about -3.67). Full method: Step 1, subtract x: 3x + 8 = -3. Step 2, subtract 8: 3x = -11. Step 3, divide: x = -11/3. Check: 4(-11/3) + 8 = -20/3 and -11/3 - 3 = -20/3. Takeaway: collect x on the side with the larger coefficient, and carry the sign all the way through.

items.stem: Two solutions are mixed in a ratio of 4 to 3 by volume to make 14 mL. How many mL of the solution with the smaller share are used?
items.why: Fastest: 7 parts in 14 mL is 2 mL per part; the smaller share is 3 parts = 6 mL. Full method: the smaller share is 3 of 4 + 3 = 7 parts: (3/7)(14) = 6 mL. Check: 8 + 6 = 14 and 8 : 6 = 4 : 3. Takeaway: add the parts for the whole, find one part, then scale.

items.stem: Events A and B have P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.2, and P(A and B) = 0.01. What is P(A or B)?
items.why: Fastest: or = add, minus the overlap: 0.3 + 0.2 - 0.01 = 0.49. Full method: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). The overlap is inside both P(A) and P(B), so it is subtracted once: 0.49. Takeaway: OR adds and then removes the double-counted overlap; AND is the overlap itself.

items.stem: For what value of k does the equation x^2 + 6x + k = 0 have exactly one real solution?
items.why: Fastest: a perfect square: x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)^2 has the single root -3, so k = 9. Full method: one real solution means the discriminant is zero: b^2 - 4ac = 36 - 4(1)(k) = 0, so k = 9. Takeaway: discriminant positive, two real roots; zero, one; negative, none. For x^2 + bx + k, one root means k = (b/2)^2.

items.stem: What are all the solutions of 2x^2 - 18 = 0?
items.why: Fastest: 2x^2 = 18, so x^2 = 9 and x = 3 or -3. Full method: Step 1, add 18: 2x^2 = 18. Step 2, divide by 2: x^2 = 9. Step 3, take both square roots: x = 3 or x = -3. (Factoring agrees: 2(x - 3)(x + 3) = 0.) Takeaway: isolate x^2 completely, then remember both the positive and negative roots.

items.stem: What is the sum of the solutions of x^2 + 5x - 14 = 0?
items.why: Fastest: for x^2 + bx + c, the roots add to -b: here -5. Full method: factor: (x + 7)(x - 2) = 0, so x = -7 or x = 2. Sum = -5. (Their product is -14, the constant term.) Takeaway: the roots of x^2 + bx + c add to -b and multiply to c.

items.stem: What is the value of the discriminant of 2x^2 - 3x - 5 = 0?
items.why: Fastest: b^2 - 4ac = 9 - 4(2)(-5) = 9 + 40 = 49. Full method: a = 2, b = -3, c = -5. b^2 = 9; 4ac = 4(2)(-5) = -40; b^2 - 4ac = 9 + 40 = 49. A positive perfect square means two rational roots (here 5/2 and -1). Takeaway: write a, b and c with their signs before you substitute; a negative c makes -4ac positive.

items.stem: A tank holds 4,000 liters of water. A drain removes 7 liters per minute while a pipe adds 3 liters per minute. Starting full, how many minutes will it take for the tank to empty?
items.why: Fastest: net loss is 7 - 3 = 4 liters per minute, so 4,000 / 4 = 1,000 minutes. Full method: rate out minus rate in = 4 L/min. Time = amount / net rate = 4,000 / 4 = 1,000 minutes. Takeaway: opposing rates subtract; then time = amount / net rate.

items.stem: If 3^(2x - 1) = 27, what is the value of x?
items.why: Fastest: 27 = 3^3, so the exponents match: 2x - 1 = 3 and x = 2. Full method: Step 1, write both sides with base 3: 3^(2x - 1) = 3^3. Step 2, equal bases mean equal exponents: 2x - 1 = 3. Step 3, x = 2. Check: 3^3 = 27. Takeaway: rewrite both sides with the same base, then set the exponents equal.

items.stem: A bag contains 5 red marbles and 7 blue marbles. Three marbles are drawn WITHOUT replacement. What is the probability that exactly 2 are red and 1 is blue?
items.why: Fastest: C(5,2) x C(7,1) / C(12,3) = (10 x 7) / 220 = 70/220 = 7/22. Full method: total groups of 3 from 12 = 220. Choose 2 of the 5 red (10 ways) and 1 of the 7 blue (7 ways): 70 favorable. 70/220 = 7/22. (By order: 3 x (5/12)(4/11)(7/10) = 7/22.) Takeaway: exactly k of one kind means multiply the combinations for each kind, over the total combinations.

items.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 6 hours. Pipe B fills the same tank in 9 hours. Pipe C empties the tank in 12 hours. If all three pipes are open simultaneously, how long does it take to fill the empty tank?
items.why: Fastest: use a 36-unit tank. A adds 6 units per hour, B adds 4, C removes 3: net 7 units per hour, so 36/7 hours (about 5.1). Full method: net rate = 1/6 + 1/9 - 1/12 = 6/36 + 4/36 - 3/36 = 7/36 tank per hour. Time = 36/7 hours. Takeaway: fillers add rates, drains subtract them; then flip the net rate to get the time.

items.stem: A right triangle has legs of length 3 and 4 (and hypotenuse 5). It is inscribed in a CIRCLE such that the hypotenuse is a diameter. What is the area of the region INSIDE the circle but OUTSIDE the triangle?
items.why: Fastest: radius = 5/2, circle = 25 pi/4, triangle = 6, difference = 25 pi/4 - 6 (about 13.6). Full method: Step 1, the hypotenuse is a diameter, so r = 2.5. Step 2, circle area = pi(2.5)^2 = 25 pi/4. Step 3, triangle area = (1/2)(3)(4) = 6. Step 4, region = 25 pi/4 - 6. Takeaway: a right triangle in a circle has its hypotenuse as the diameter; halve it before squaring.

items.stem: A solution that is 25% acid by volume is mixed with a solution that is 60% acid. To produce 35 liters of a final solution that is 40% acid, how many liters of the 25% solution must be used?
items.why: Fastest: seesaw. 40 is 15 from 25 and 20 from 60, so 25-percent : 60-percent = 20 : 15 = 4 : 3. 4/7 of 35 = 20 L. Full method: let x be liters of 25 percent; 35 - x is liters of 60 percent. Acid: 0.25x + 0.60(35 - x) = 0.40(35) = 14. So 21 - 0.35x = 14, giving x = 20 L. Takeaway: the larger share sits closer to the target strength; check it with the acid equation.

items.stem: In a dataset of 7 numbers, the mean is 12 and the median is 10. Each number is increased by 5. What are the new mean and median?
items.why: Fastest: adding a constant slides the whole data set, so every center moves by that constant: 17 and 15. Full method: new mean = (sum + 7 x 5) / 7 = old mean + 5 = 17. The order of the values does not change, so the middle value also rises by 5: 15. Takeaway: adding c shifts mean, median and mode by c and leaves the spread alone; multiplying by c scales all of them.

items.stem: A lab raises its weekly sample count by 20 percent, then reduces the new count by 25 percent, ending at 90 samples per week. What was the original weekly count?
items.why: Fastest: net factor 1.2 x 0.75 = 0.9, so the original is 90 / 0.9 = 100. Full method: original C. After the rise: 1.20C. After the cut: 0.75(1.20C) = 0.90C = 90, so C = 100. Check: 100, then 120, then 90. Takeaway: combine the percent changes into one factor, then divide to work backward.
